transcript.content: Well, absolutely. What can I say? Yeah, great.
Um, you didn't go to Pulp in the park yesterday, did you?
This is, uh, my mate Jarvis. This is Pulp and “Common People”. What?
No, I know. What about pen pals? You say pen pals, don't you? You don't meet them, but they're friends.
Yeah, but you've never had any contact with Jarvis whatsoever. Gervais, I don't know anything about this. What was it? What was going on?
This was a big event? Was it a big- some big gig?
Oh, you asked. What were you doing?
Making some more clogs for the disco?
Hey! Maybe I was with a lady.
Anyway, I've met—I've met Jarvis before. Met him at ULU at the Longpigs gig, 'cause he's mates with 'em.
He's sort of thin. Got glasses.
Well, he has success with ladies. Why don't I?
Yeah. You don't want to go into that? Do you want—no, I don't think we should.
Tell me about it. So what was it? I don't understand. You were involved somewhere, weren't you?
Yeah. Well, just go out and say, “Ladies and gentlemen, give it up for,” you know...
What did you do? I mean, what—what—what was your shtick?
Well, I wanted to go out and interrupt Jarvis with a Michael Jackson mask on.
So I did it to Catatonia instead.
Yeah, don't really work, does it?
Didn't have the same impact at all.
Who else was on? Bernard Butler, was he?

Yeah, oh, Bernard Butler. I had a lovely little trick ready. I borrowed a little peaked cap off of this and John's ambulance, and I was getting ready to go out and go, oh, I hate you, Butler, get that bus out now.
But they played an intro tape, and I told him, he said, oh, it's a shame, that would have been funny.
So lots of opportunities there, wasted.
But I did go out when...
Very much the story of your life, Gervais.
Yeah. When the roadies were going, “A bit more dB on that. I need a—” I did go and get me arse out.
You hadn't got your arse out?
Right, because the classy stuff wasn't working.
No, I had to sort of like dumb it down a little bit.
Yeah, yeah. That's the nature of those audiences.
But it's funny, right, because, hold on, I'm getting bored now, it's Catatonia, they were on.
No idea. One thing I would say though, if anyone saw Ricky yesterday at, uh, where was it, Finsbury Park?
01715802000. Was he faintly amusing? What did he get up to? Gervais,
You know last week we started a competition where people had to send in photographs or pictures or anything.
Um, if, uh, I would show them to you indiscriminately during the show and see if you would laugh.
Well, it could have been. It could have been.
I did that myself. But that's the idea.
That's the idea. Fax- Can I just say, fax-
I admit, I- I drew that one, but-
Wait a minute, wait a minute.
And I could never—I—not only could I not tell them what that was, I could never explain it well enough.
No. So- There's nothing you could do to explain that picture.
Suffice to say, if you've got a picture that you think can make old Gervais laugh, and we will hopefully give a prize to, to somebody somewhere during the show.
It's specifics like that that make this show. Sort of. You know what I mean?
The vague promise that there might be a prize.
Anyway, if you have a picture that you think, er, can make Gervais laugh, 0171580...
Shut up, I'm trying to give the number here. 0171580...
That—yeah, exactly. How are they gonna phone in a drawing?
It's simple things, Gervais, that let you down.
Gervais, we've had a few faxes, um, and, uh, phone calls, because people did see you, apparently, yesterday, at, uh, Finsbury Park.
Introducing the bands. We've had a, a number of callers. Uh, let me just sort of tell you what they've said. They've passed this information on to us.
It's going to be hurtful, isn't it?
Well, you know, all I would say, Gervais, is you mock me, all right, about my appearance.
Okay, 'cause you—you know you're safe. People don't know what you look like 'cause you're on the wireless.
You've made a big, big error.
Alright, Les called. He said Ricky let himself down by mooning. Gervais, all I'd say to you is...
No, I did sort of a roadie's cleavage.
The point is, Gervais, you see, even... I- I mean, those are classics in your repertoire.
Aren't they? Getting your arse out. That's like your sort of, um, you know, the very best of Woody Allen, you know. That's like one of his hour-long monologues. That's yours, isn't it?
I didn't do the fish though, did I? That's my pièce de résistance.
Well, I don't know about that.
Anyway, Claire has also phoned in.

Um, Claire has phoned in. She said, “You're a bit large,” all right? “You had a haircut”—don't know what that means—“and you're quieter than on the radio.” Any reason? What, what, what was going on? Why weren't you shouting and bawling?
Well, all I'd say- well, I'd point you in the-
I'd point you in the direction of a bit large, Gervais, because that leads nicely onto the uh, the final call here from Katie.
Fatter than I- Fatter than I thought, Gervais, but still gorgeous.
So it's interesting there that they've spotted that you're quite a fat and uh, talentless man.
I'm not that fat, am I?
Well, no, but two people of those three calls have pointed out the fact that you're fat.
And the other one, all he could see was your arse. So, Gervais, I just—you’re a little bit disappointed, I imagine. You're probably feeling a little bit low, a bit shocked.
You thought that the TV contracts would be flooding in, but...
It's—it's not my media, really, just sort of rock festival.
Well, I—I was—I went there, right, and first of all there was a lot of noise.
Right, I'm walking around. It was hot, which I liked. I sort of laid down. But I—I didn't take any sun cream, so after about four hours I was—I was getting a bit warm.
And I was knackered 'cause I was having to work.
I had to keep going on—keep going on stage, which I wanted to sort of sit in one place near the chemical toilet, between the chemical toilet and the bar, or incorporate those...
In one sort of strange invention, which I'm going to do one day.
Yeah, yeah, yeah. We've- We've all been there.
In one end, out the other.

And, um, so I was sitting there, and then this—someone came, a friend of ours had some, um, uh, factor so-and-so, fifty or summat. I put it on, and Becky, Ben's Becky, was there with some lip balm. I put that on so, you know, it wouldn't crack.

Um, and it was all okay. But then, as I started getting a little bit more out of it, we were sort of like drinking and enjoying ourselves, and I was hot, and I got a runny eye. My eyes started stinging. And I was going, “Oh, me eye,” and I was tired, and I was losing heat through me sunburn. It was getting cold, and I put me tracksuit top on, white tracksuit top. So there I was sitting.

And also then, about a couple of hours later, the lip balm came out again. I had a flashback. I remember the first time it went round. It was like in a film, I had a flashback. And as I—I realised the—I'd put it on my lips, then put a little bit on my eyelids!
In case of, um- in case of chapped eyelids?
No, I thought it might cool them down.
And that- then I realised, oh, that's why my eyes are stinging.
So I'm there with runny eyes. I'm tired. I'm a little bit drunk. I'm in a white tracksuit with shades on. I had turned into Jimmy Savile.
Yeah. And I saw all these kids looking at me thinking, “Oh, bless him.” And going, “You all right? Where's the toilet?” “You've done it.” Going, “Nah.” No...
Dear Jimmy, I am four years old and I have a terminal illness. Can you fix it for me to live a long and healthy life? Well, no, but we have arranged it for you to do a duet with Mr. Shaking Stevens.
“I feel sick.” “This Ole House, do it, you little b—” “I f—I feel sick, Mummy. It's the treatment.” Anyway.
What's behind the green door? A cure? No. No,
No, no. He's for comas. He's not for terminal illness. He gets people out of comas, doesn't he, Shakin' Stevens?

He does. He—apparently, loads of kids in the eighties, they're all on there, all these people going, “Oh yeah, and she was in a coma, and we played Shakin' Stevens twenty-four hours a day and she—” I'd come out of it if someone—I'd be like, “Turn that...
Shit off! Know what I mean,
Who would you least like to visit you if you were in a coma?

Imagine it, right, you're—you're in a coma, yeah? You're in a catatonic—you've got all your senses. You've got all your senses except sight. You can't do a thing, right? And you've got someone there to come and visit you. You're helpless.
I'm just sort of lying on a bed.
But you can—you can feel... I'll tell you who I wouldn't want to visit me. Jason Donovan.
Not- I don't like his voice.
Or Philip Schofield, don't like his singing voice.
No, but I wouldn't want him round. I wouldn't want him round.
No, I don't know, it's just something about him. Something about him.
Um, anyway, we've got some Skunk Anansie coming up.
So- and I'll tell you who else I want. Village People.
Bring the four of them, Rick.
[Sings] Y-M-C- Four of 'em? What- what one d'you wanna leave out? There was five of 'em.
Village, everyone knows there's four village people.
Alright, wait a minute, so there's a- there's a fire, no, hang on, there's a there's a- there's a road cop.
Um, There's a red Indian, obviously.
And there's a construction worker, and there's something else. There's something—a chef? No, a candle—
At the back with those little half-moon glasses. “Y.M.C.A.” Do a little bit of sewing.
Who was it? Hang on, wait a minute. There was a fire chief.
What are you on about? There was no—
No, there weren't a fire chief. There was a- a police...
The black guy was a road cop- a traffic cop.
There was a red Indian. Obviously.
Yeah, there was a a- a construction worker.
Yeah, course there was a cowboy!
Well, who was the fifth one, then?

I don't know if there was. I might've made that up. Maybe I just dreamt one. I thought of maybe some—maybe a bloke dressed up as Judy Garland. It's about, um, half four, Sunday. Ricky Gervais Show. I'm Ricky Gervais.
Well, it's interesting. We had a call from a fellow called Paul Murray.
And Paul tells me that there are, or rather there were, perhaps there still are, six village people.
That's more than I remember. Go on, then.
Um, but what's interesting is Paul here, uh, has managed to name every single member of that squad, plus the different roles that they played.
And what I'm intrigued to know is, like, most people can't even name all four Smiths, all right?
Or decent bands, even, you know, maybe all four Rolling Stones. Uh, sorry, all six—five Rolling Stones. However many there are.
Yeah. But, uh, but this man can name all six village people and the roles they played.
One wonders about his musical taste.

Anyway, um, the cowboy, Gervais, you might—might want to make a note. The cowboy was played by Victor Willis. There was a Red Indian. He was David Hodo. Uh, Felipe Rose played the policeman. Randy Jones was a GI, a soldier. Uh, Glenn Hughes played the biker.
And uh, Alex Briley was the construction worker. Six village people. Gervais.
So, in, in, you know, in Trivial Pursuit or any of the...
That would be crowded, though, wouldn't it, in the ward?
I bet that matron'd be coming round saying, “What is this? Get out! Get out! He can't hear you.” “I think he can. He's—he flickers a little bit every now and again.”
So, yeah, we're taking your calls on, um, on who you'd least like to have visiting you uh, when you're in a coma.
Maybe you could have a special donor card. Like, um, in a case of me falling into a catatonic state where I can still hear a bit, don't let Shakin' Stevens in.

Do you know what I mean? Or, see, my girlfriend knows exactly what I'd want. I'd want 24 um, hours a day, Derek and Clive, with bits of, like, Radiohead and the Smiths sort of, like, you know, mixed into it. Do you know what I mean?
That'd be easy. She'd know. But you can't always rely on that.

I mean, who would you turn to? There's no one would want to come near you when you're sort of like walking around. Maybe you wouldn't be so scary when you're sort of like unconscious. I don't know, actually, you'd probably be worse, wouldn't you?
Because you'd have your glasses off, because you wouldn't need them, and they sort of help you, they humanise you, I'll be honest.
Can you imagine imagine all the nurses in their staff room, no, I'm not going in.
Drawing straws. “No, I’m not going anywhere near him.”
No, and you'd probably have some sort of drip thing, wouldn't you?
And that just, that just sort of keeps you alive, that's all the protein and everything you need. Imagine Dawn French visiting you.
She'd be there for a while, and the nurse comes in, why isn't his drip connected? She goes,
We had a call from, uh, Heather and Jim. They, uh, they apparently met you once before and they said you're not quite as fat as they remember.
Sorry, not quite as fat as everyone was suggesting.
See, I'm not fat. What I've done is I've let myself go a little bit around the midriff, you see? So, in this, like, indie world of being Seven Stone, of course, I'm suddenly ape man, aren't I?
Yeah. These youngsters, “Oh, what's that?” It's this beer gut. You'll get it. You'll get it, all right? My—my jawline's not as chiselled as it used to be.
Well, it's not so much a jawline...
No, not really. It's a pelican.
Yeah. Yeah, it goes straight into it.
Heather and Jim, they said that they didn't really fancy Nick Cave popping round when they've got—when they're in a coma. I don't know, I wouldn't have a problem with that.
He could bring some of his, uh, bring some of his H along.

Xfm 104.9, Ricky Gervais Show. Don't forget, keep, um, faxing in the people you'd least like, or most like, to visit you in a coma and what you'd like played to you. So, you know, I think this is twenty-four hours a day. Maybe learn to speak French.

You know what I mean? You come out and you're fine. You know what I mean? That would be great because there's nothing else to do. So, all those things you thought of you know, doing like, and maybe a martial art, that would be difficult.
Yeah. How to chat out women.
I'd have to be in a coma for a lot longer.
Uh, Yeah, two things, Gervais. One, you know, last week I mentioned that I've got a celebrity relation.
I'm going to be mentioning uh, that in a second, so bear with me because it's an exciting thing, obviously. I've got I've got a celebrity relation. Gervais.
It's not very exciting. It's not very intriguing, but I think you'll be—
They're going, “Oh God, please don't. The phones are gonna go.” Get an injunction out on it.
0171 580 2000. Have you got an interesting celebrity relation? Also, Gervais, are you gonna mention the compilation tape?

Oh yeah, I was thinking of, like, doing a little compilation tape. Like, we'd play, like, some of our most loved and beautiful tunes. You could pick three, and we could play 'em back to back with no little segueing, no little idents, and no speaking over the intro or outro, so they could tape 'em.
Well, yeah, no, I'll stop you there, Gervais, because I think the idea's great.
But obviously it is against the law for anybody to tape...

So get the—get it ready, and we'll tell you when, and then we leave a little gap, so press that record, and then you can have three in a row. Like I'd choose something like, I think I'd choose, um, “Let Down” off, uh, OK Computer, and that'd go nicely into, um, “Suffer Little Children” by the Smiths, and then finish with, um, “After the Gold Rush”, Neil Young. Three there. And then, you know, next week I'll play another three.
Like, what would you play, your three?
Well, I'd probably play something by, uh, I don't know, who knows, R.E.M. maybe?
A bit of R.E.M., a classic, some New Order or somebody like that.
So, yours would be more like a sort of classic indie dance.
The Happy Mondays, the Happy Mondays.
Yeah. Sort of, Party. Party. Yeah.
But of course, I would stress again, Gervais, that it is against the law.
For people to hit play and record and tape those tracks.
So we're doing that a bit later. So get your, um, get a blank cassette now. Um, and we'll be doing that, what? So we'll be doing that at about five?
Well, obviously we won't be doing it because it is against the law.
Okay. We'll do that at five then. Um, after the break, Terrorvision. Xfm, London's only alternative.
What's that? Janet... What's that say? Janet Crawley dressed as a woman.
Oh, yeah. It's your writing, isn't it? Janet Cranky dressed as a woman rather than a small child.
I know. Don't you think that's my worst nightmare?
Oh God. Dr Fox. Oh, that's—hmm, don't know about Dr Fox. Um, Whitney Houston. That's harsh, but fair.
Dressed as a... Maybe trying to look a bit beautiful.

I know, that's what I can't understand. But what was he thinking? Did he see her and chat her up in a club or something, and then later discover that she looks great dressed as a boy? Or did they start off...
They were at that sort of club.
Did they start off doing that shtick?
We'll leave it there. We'll leave it there!
He wouldn't have said that. He knew it was a woman. He only likes the company and sex with women. No, it's just her. It's his wife. So... No!
How could you only... How could you fall in love with that woman?
Look at the woman. She's short. She's squat. She's weird looking.
If there's a chance for her...
Maybe—maybe I just need to start dressing up as schoolchildren.

Oh, think of that. We're going to start off now, so get ready to press play and record on your tape. This is Steve's little compilation. We're going to kick off with a secret track by R.E.M., aren't we?
That's right, but can I just stress again that you shouldn't hit play and record because, of course, it is illegal to do so.
Okay, I'm gonna, um, fade myself down now, so there'll be no talking on this bit, okay?

Well, that was three in a row there. That's Steve's choice for your compilation tape. R.E.M., Electronic and Gomez. But Steve, read out... Spell it for them and read out the title so they can get a pen and write it down for the label of the cassette.
No, no, I told you before, Gervais, it's illegal for them to have taped those songs.
What- so what was it? It was R.E.M.-
No, we... Alright, you can take these down, but do not write them in the inlay card of the Ricky Gervais compilation because you're not allowed.
Alright? It's as simple as that.
But the three tracks, just for your own knowledge...
Okay? And if you've got a pen handy and you need to take them down, then grab a pen now. But the three tracks were “Superwoman”...
How are you spelling that, Steve?
Capital R, I should say. Capital E. Capital M.
And that's a secret track on the album Lifes Rich Pageant.
The second track was a classic single from Electronic.
Spelling that in the usual manner.
And the track was Getting Away With It.
No, it's not. No, it's not. It's getting away with it.
And Finally, there, of course, Gomez from their current album and the track Get Myself Arrested.
On XFM 104.9, just gone, five o'clock. Little boy Fraser was on the phone to do with Steve's compilation. He says, well, one, that REM track is called Superman, not Superwoman, okay?
And two, it's clearly listed on the CD itself. It's not a secret track at all.
I'll stop you there, Gervais. I'll stop you there straight away, all right? Now, Little Boy Fraser, for those who don't know, he's sort of one of the big sort of music bods here, right?
He sort of is involved with the library of records. He's to do with the playlist, all the rest of it.
He's 16 years old and his mum, he wants to come in every day, but his mum says, no, you've got to have a day off. You don't get paid, they're taking you for a ride.
Exactly. And even though he's very young, he claims to know a lot about music. Yeah. But I'll tell you, here, he's embarrassed himself. Right? I've got the CD.
I've got the CD in front of me. Now, I don't know which issue or which—you know, I'm sure he's got the original vinyl release.
That's signed by the band or whatever. I'm looking at the copy here, right? And this one tallies with the copy I've got at home, Gervais.

I'm opening up the CD here. I'm looking at the sleeve, which I assume, and I'll be honest, I am assuming, is a reproduction of the original sleeve, you know, the original artwork. Right. And you'll notice that nowhere does it mention the track Super Woman, as I like to call it.
You'll notice that it's got all uh, ten, ten tracks there.
And the, that, the last track you'll notice...
Steve seems to be right, It's just got a little plus.
Suggesting there might be another hidden track.
Clue, yeah, he's in the plus. Oh, well, Little Boy Fraser seems to be wrong now.
So on the sleeve, you'll notice there's no mention...
He's taken off his dad's shower suit and throwing it down in disgust. He's just left there in his pants at the moment.
There's no mention of the track on the...
The only mention of the track itself is on the CD.
They've listed all, um, all the, uh, twelve tracks.
I'm just gonna confirm this. And it says Superwoman.
Well, Little Boy Fraser seems to be embarrassing himself.
Now, I don't know, you see, maybe he's right, Maybe in the great scheme of things, Stipe has suggested that it's actually called Superman, and that it's not to be known as a hidden track,
But I'm just going by the facts, the evidence, Gervais. 0171 580 2000. Whose side are you on?
Who's right? Little Boy Incontinent Fraser or Ugly Boy Lizard Man Steve? The choice is yours.
Yeah, well, let's not, y'know, let's not sort of try and bias the vote, if we can, all right?
Okay, yeah, 'cause they'd fall for that. But what do they write on the inlay of their cassette, the people who've been taping it?
Well, that's very much- that's very much the difficult question at the moment, and, uh, that's hopefully what, um, perhaps Michael Stipe or, um, or one of the other-
Well, I've caught you out because they shouldn't be writing anything 'cause they shouldn't be taping off the radio, Steve.
"If You'll Be Mine" by Babybird. Steve's singing along there to Babybird, which is ironic, because when you sing, you're putting your head back and your mouth's open, you look like a baby bird.
Yeah, 'cause the long neck and that sort of goitre thing you've got. You look like a sort of- like a fledgling pelican.
And the worms, of course, hanging from my mouth.
Yeah. But it's- it's ironic as well because- 'cause you're, like, Lizoidian as well. You- you're-
Because you're a Lizoidian. Oh, right, of course.
Don't. Because I use... I sometimes forget that they're not real words.
You sometimes forget that your language comes from the voices inside your head.
I use my own language. They tell me what to say and I say it.
No, listen. It's sort of like a little, little bird-like lizoidian thing, right? Which is like the Archaeopteryx. Like the, the link between—from a sort of lizard man going, “Flight.”
They've kicked in again. They've kicked in early. Oh. They're not meant to start for about an hour.
No, the tablets. Right, go on.
Anyway, you know that I put out that little appeal there. I wanted to find out if my, um, my view of the R.E.M. track “Superwoman” was correct, or whether Little Boy Fraser was right.
Uh, is Emma still there? Has Emma disappeared?
She's gone. She's got the—she's got the results.

She's got the stats there, and we've had calls coming in saying who's right. Um, oh, hang on. So Emma, you can corroborate it. Who—who was right there? Who was right? Was it me or was it Little Boy Fraser?
And I believe I'm right in saying that no calls came in supporting Fraser.
No, you're right. You are right, yeah.
But why do you gloat over a little kid who's—is, like, helping us out, doesn't get paid for it, has got a problem with his intestines, his bowel movements?
I'll tell you, right, you don't argue with me.
He goes through shell suits like Liverpudlians and, you know, you're... he's sitting there now, he's probably taking off his pants angry, he's just got his mum's shoes on now and he's furious.
Fraser, Fraser, a little word of advice, right? Don't start on me until you've got pubic hair.
That is so, at least he's got a girlfriend.
At least he's got a girlfriend. That old lady with the flat head and no teeth outside Goodge Street station.
Anyway, listen, before we carry on...
Um, also, I want... My celebrity... My celebrity relation. I want to mention that in a second.
Um, and something else... You've got something else, haven't you?
Oh, I've got my um, three compilations that you can tape off the radio.
Don't don't tape them, because they're illegal.
No, this is my… one of my favourite tracks that we've ever put on the, uh, the playlist. This is, uh, Robert Pollard and Make Use.
Let's hear it, let's hear it.
Xfm 104.9, just coming up to quarter past five. Well, this isn't looking so good, uh, for you, Steve.

Um, because, uh, one guy's faxed in, “On my copies of Lifes Rich—Lifes Rich Pageant, the track you played earlier is listed as ‘Superman’, not ‘Superwoman’, on the CD. R.E.M. manufacturing different editions of the album, or yet more gender problems on your show?”
And there's another guy phoned and said definitely, definitely, Fraser is right. He's got it on vinyl, and I think vinyl wins over CDs. So Fraser has won.
Wait, wait, wait a minute. Wait a minute.

No, that's—no, I'm not gonna settle for that, for goodness' sake. It's just, it's just once again an example of the fact you can't—you can't let me get, you know, anything. You can't let me win anything on this bloody show.
No, because you don't deserve it, because you're a horrible little amphiboloid sort of...
Yeah, little creature, little lizoidian scale-creck.
That doesn't—that doesn't, Gervais, wipe out the fact that...
I'm correct as far as R.E.M.'s concerned. We've had a lot of calls supporting me.
Until we get word of, until we get word...
Until we get word from REM themselves, all right, clearing this out I'm not taking no for an answer.
I wish I knew what that sentence meant.
I'm not gonna say anything there.
I may as well tell you now, 'cause-
I've been trailing it and it's not that exciting.
It's really not that exciting. But anyway, my celebrity- my celebrity relation is... drumroll, please!
No, er, it's not Godzilla. Right-
Who is it? What's the relation first?
Second cousin. Now, what is that?
I don't know. Maybe it's third cousin.
In, in Bristol, that can be sister, can't it?
So she's your second or third cousin?
I mean, she—she doesn't know who I am, but I know who she is.
Anyone from the Bananas listening, give us a call. Deny it. Embarrass him again.
No, this is true, this. She was a bridesmaid at my mother's wedding.
Yeah, they—they are—they are blonde-haired at one time, except for Karen, who was replaced by another darker... How many are in Bananarama now? They're back together again, aren't they?
No! I know. I'll play an ad break and then Swervedriver. I had a whole new idea.
Yeah. After this ad break, I'm gonna press this button.
Well, I've got you, Steve. You've been proved wrong.

No you have you have, beyond doubt. Little Boy Fraser's called up and uh, Dan Sayer called independently to um, back this up. Um, It's not even an REM song. They've covered it. By, um, It's a band called the, uh, The Clique, a psychedelic band from the uh, late 60s, early 70s, um, and it was called Superman.
So I don't care what REM say, it's called Superman.
I'll stop you there, Gervais, right?
The fact that R.E.M. are now calling it “Superwoman”, right?
All right? If they wanna get together and have a scrap, that's fair enough.
So—so if I completely cover a song exactly the same, just cover it like, um, “Love, Love Me Don't” by the Beatles, that's fine, is it? “Love, Love Me Don't.”
Gervais, whoa! Listen, just shut up for a second.
“Sheila in the Sky with Diamonds” by Ricky Gervais.
Shut up for just one second, right?
The argument was, what should people put on their cassette tape compilation inlay card?
